native_mechanisms: Silence-swats: every mark is laid on its own flat stone so the input's order/position is fixed before any heap is folded.
Each heap races the musk deer's mountain stride — uphill twist, downhill fold, doubling back — so no heap keeps the shape it entered with, with the running shape carried into the next heap.
The owl seals the final folded shape to one fixed small size and burns every intermediate heap, so the token cannot be walked back to its marks.
Searching in squares: turn the shape ninety degrees and fold its corners into its own centre, repeatedly, until one changed mark smears across every square.
core_technique: Wide 1024-bit state as a 4x4 grid of 64-bit lanes: each 8-byte word XOR'd into its own positional lane, then per-row rotate-plus-xorshift followed by a 90-degree lane permutation and ChaCha-style add/xor/rotate corner folding (AVX2-vectorised, dual cursors reading from both ends), with a murmur3 fmix64 finalizer — multiplication-free bulk ARX permutation, not single-accumulator multiply-xor folding.
notes: The bulk loop deliberately contains no multiply (unlike FNV-1a/xxHash); deer_stride is the rotate/xor-shift stride, sq_mix is the ninety-degree turn plus corner fold, mechanism 1 survives as positional lane placement and mechanism 3 as the fmix64 seal over a one-way 16-to-1 lane collapse — but the executed core is mechanism 2 (plus its square-fold companion, item 4).
